$description: aitmproxy operator-UI design tokens. Single source of truth for the macOS app, the web UI and the terminal UI. Every surface maps these names to its platform (SwiftUI Color/Font/CGFloat, CSS custom properties, ratatui Style). Values derive from Proxyman's WebUI (light) and native dashboard (dark), reconciled into one system; see docs/design/operator-ui-foundation.md §2 for the rationale and §2.9 for the TUI mapping rules.

color.$description: Every color has a light and a dark value. Text tiers hold 4.5:1 or better on the surface they sit on. 'tui' is the nearest ANSI-16 name for terminals that cannot show truecolor; truecolor terminals use the dark hex.

page.$description: Window/page background behind panels (WebUI off-white; native near-black).

surface.$description: Panels, the flow table, inspector panes.

raised.$description: Chips, inset wells, the status bar, sidebar group headers.

active.$description: Selected row in a list that drives a detail pane; selected sidebar item. A quiet accent tint, never the full accent.

hover.$description: Row/item hover. Never moves a selection.

inverse.$description: Near-black primary button fill (light) / inverted white (dark).

border.$description: Panel edges, pane splitters, the rule under tab bars.

rule.$description: Row separators in tables and key-value lists; one step lighter than border.

control.$description: Input, select and outlined-button borders; one step darker than border.

primary.$description: Identity text: URL host, header names, values, titles. Increase-Contrast pushes it to pure black/white.

tertiary.$description: Placeholders, meta, disabled labels. Floor of the readable tiers (4.7:1 on raised, 5.3:1 on surface in light).

link.$description: URL path segment and links: the accent's deep shade in light so it holds 4.5:1 on the selected-row tint; the WebUI draws the path in a blue-violet, we keep one hue.

base.$description: THE accent: active tab underline, focus ring, selection tint source, primary links, the product mark. Taken from Proxyman WebUI's active-tab blue. Budget: about 3% of pixels.

deep.$description: Accent text on light surfaces / pressed state.

tint.$description: Accent wash: selected row, GET badge background.

intercept.$description: The breakpoint/intercept state. Amber: Proxyman's 'Active' badge and breakpoint accent, mitmproxy's highlighted intercepted row. The ONLY place a saturated fill with on-color text is allowed on chrome, because an armed intercept is the one state the operator must never miss.

agent.$description: The AI agent's presence over MCP. Teal: distinct from every method/status hue so an agent-authored action is unmistakable. Used on the Agent toggle, the left-edge tick on agent-originated flows (replays, PoC runs), and agent entries in the activity log. Shared with no other role.

l4.$description: Raw L4 (transport-layer) flows: capture, craft, inject, in-path intercept. Slate/indigo, deliberately distinct from accent-blue, intercept-amber, agent-teal and WS-violet so an L4 session and its TCP/UDP/ICMP sub-label read as their own protocol family. Used on the L4 kind badge, the packet/layer/hex inspector chrome and the craft editor. OQ1 (ui-scripting-highlight-l4) resolved to slate/indigo.

badge.$description: The L4 kind badge and TCP/UDP/ICMP sub-label: tint background + deep text.

method.$description: HTTP method badge colors, Proxyman-WebUI convention. Badge = tint background + deep text, 4px radius, 11px/600 uppercase mono. Text on tint holds 4.5:1 in both modes.

status.$description: HTTP status classes. Used as text color on the status code and as the row's leading dot.

pending.$description: In flight / no response yet (Proxyman 'Active') as TEXT. Same hue family as intercept on purpose: both mean 'not finished'. The pending status DOT uses intercept.base (a graphic: 3:1 is enough).

killed.$description: Killed/aborted flow: grey + strikethrough on the URL.

severity.$description: PoC finding severity (aitm-poc Severity enum). Pill = tint bg + deep text.

state.$description: Semantic state badges (CA trust, script status): success/warning/danger/neutral. Decoupled from method/severity so a method-palette change never recolours a state badge. Hues match the current badges (no visual change). Single-word key so the generated TUI module stays snake-case.

mark.$description: The 11 flow mark colours (Proxyman's set = the macOS system colours, light/dark). Drawn as a 6×16 swatch left of # and in the mark menu; never used on chrome. TUI maps to its 8 colours (mint/teal → cyan, indigo → blue, pink → magenta).

syntax.$description: Body viewer syntax colors (JSON/XML/HTML/JS/headers), Proxyman-native-derived. One scheme for both modes via light/dark pairs.

key.$description: JSON keys, header names, XML attribute names.

keyword.$description: Rhai control keywords (fn/let/if/…); additive for code editing.

comment.$description: Line and block comments; additive for code editing.

typography.$description: Two faces, each with one job. UI = the platform's text face. Data = monospace, for every URL, header, body, time, size and id (the Proxyman-native decision: all data columns mono). TUI: the terminal font; hierarchy by bold/dim only.

size.$description: Six sizes. Dense screens set body at 13 (study: dark/dense screens use 13).

xs.$description: Badges, pills, meta chips, line numbers. Floor.

sm.$description: Column headers, labels, timestamps, status bar.

md.$description: Body in dense views: flow rows, header tables, code.

base.$description: Body in comfortable views, sidebar labels, form controls.

xl.$description: The one screen title (h1), PoC finding title.

medium.$description: Active tab, selected sidebar item, badge text.

semibold.$description: Pane titles, h1, the status code.

tabularNums.$description: On every number in a column, a timer, or a byte count.

size.$description: Fixed dimensions of the shell. Density presets move row pitch, cell padding and body size together.

dense.$description: Default for the flow list (Proxyman native ≈30).

card.$description: Two-line WebUI-style rows (method+status / URL) for narrow layouts and the web viewer.

inspectorHeader.$description: The GET · 200 OK · URL summary line.

control.$description: Button/input height in toolbars and bars.

radius.$description: Tight family (Proxyman): badges 4, controls 6, panels 8, floating 10. Nested radii step down.

pill.$description: Only the toolbar's 'Listening on host:port' status pill and chip filters.

shadow.$description: Shadows only on what floats. Resting panels get none.

motion.$description: Feedback only; nothing on screen performs an entrance. Keyboard-initiated actions (palette open/close, tab switch, row navigation) never animate. Reduced-motion drops travel, keeps opacity.

popover.$description: Menus, popovers; scale from 0.97 at the trigger's origin.

rowArrive.$description: New flows append with no animation: the list can gain 50 rows/s.

interceptPulse.$description: The armed-intercept bar's dot pulses opacity 1→0.5; stops under reduced motion.

icon.$description: Outline, 1.5px stroke, one set. macOS: SF Symbols. Web: Lucide (closest open match to SF Symbols' geometry). TUI: a fixed Unicode glyph per role, listed below.

platform.$description: How each surface consumes these tokens.
platform.mac: Fully native Swift/SwiftUI (AppKit NSTableView for the flow list). Generate Tokens.swift: Color(light:dark:) per color token (plus Increase-Contrast variants), Font per size/weight, CGFloat per space/size/radius, Animation per motion token. Accent follows the Mac's system accent when it is not Multicolor (HIG); the token is the brand default.
platform.web: Runs everywhere at native-grade fidelity and speed (recommended: SolidJS + TypeScript, TanStack Virtual, CodeMirror 6, Vite; served by `aitm web`). Generate tokens.css: :root holds the light values as --color-*, --space-*, --size-*; :root[data-theme=dark] overrides color. prefers-color-scheme sets the default.
platform.tui: Rust + ratatui, macOS and Linux. Generate tokens.rs as a ratatui Style table: truecolor terminals use the dark hex; 256/16-color terminals use the `tui` ANSI name. Spacing/size tokens collapse to character cells (row = 1 line; toolbar/status = 1 line; sidebar = 28 cols). Weight → bold; tertiary → dim; selection → reverse video in the accent. Degrades, never drops: images and the browser viewport become labelled placeholders.
